messages.subject: multiplot
parts:
Dear all

Here is a 2column file, where I plotted Distance a x-axis and Signal1
as Y-axis by using ggplot with my own defined sizes and colour. It
works pretty well!
Is there any way to plot multiple Signal columns as shown in the last
file like Signal Signal2 ... on Y-axis by using Distance as X-axis
with specific user defined colour and other settings ?

Thanx a ton
Gireesh



Distance Signal1
-10000 0.03
-9998 0.03
-9996 0.02
-9995 0.02
.......................
......
10000 0.14
*****************************************************************************
library(ggplot2)
c <- ggplot(datax, aes(Distance, Signal1))
c + stat_smooth()
c + stat_smooth(fill=”darkgrey”, colour=”red”, size=2, alpha = 0.2)
*****************************************************************************

-10000 0.03 0.12 0.9
-9998 0.03 0.4 0.6
-9996 0.02 0.22 0.2

Should be able to do it just by having a stat_smooth() for each set of Y data.

c <- ggplot(datax, aes(x=Distance))

c+
stat_smooth(aes(y=Signal1), fill=”darkgrey”, colour=”red”, size=2, alpha = 0.2)+
stat_smooth(aes(y=Signal2), fill=”grey80”, colour=”blue”, size=2, alpha = 0.2)

If it starts to get too complex consider using reshape/melt.

datax2 <- melt(datax, id.vars=Distance)

d <- ggplot(datax, aes(x=Distance, y=value))

d + stat_smooth(aes(colour = variable), size = 2, alpha = 0.2)
